evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 雨: oracle-bone form description and earliest cited uses
evidence.text: The entry describes variable oracle-bone forms: a top stroke may represent sky, with two or three drops beneath; drops sometimes touch the upper stroke, and another stroke may be decorative. It cites 《合集》8329 and 20397 for noun uses meaning rainwater, and 《合集》9757 and 12598 for verbal uses meaning ‘to rain’. These are early inscription references, but the page does not date each cited record. It also describes Western Zhou forms with the outer rain shape connected, and Warring States forms where drops can resemble water.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 漢字甲骨部件分析 雨

evidence.text: The page indexes 雨 under oracle-bone script, bronze inscriptions (including 集成01717), Chu slips, small seal and Shuowen forms. Its summary describes the graph as rainwater dripping downward. The parsed page does not expose the individual glyph drawings or their dates.
evidence.title: 漢字「雨」：字形演變

evidence.field: File description, provenance and reuse terms for 雨-seal.svg
evidence.text: The exact file page describes the image as 雨 in Shuowen seal-script style and names Sinica Database and Chinese Etymology among its sources. It states that the Sinica database picture is CC0 1.0 and the displayed SVG is released under CC0/public-domain terms. This is a modern digital vector reconstruction, not a photograph or direct image of an ancient artifact. The page links the original file at https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b0/%E9%9B%A8-seal.svg; the browser could not render the SVG as a page.
evidence.title: File:雨-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

search_audit.query: 雨 oracle bone inscriptions graph evolution Academia Sinica 雨 甲骨 金文 字形
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the Academia Sinica evolution page and CUHK entry. Search results also surfaced Wiktionary, the Chinese Text Project and Oraclebone.org; no further claim is based on those result snippets.

search_audit.query: 雨-seal.svg Wikimedia Commons File 雨 seal; Shuowen Seal Radical 422.svg Wikimedia Commons
search_audit.outcome: Opened the exact Commons page for 雨-seal.svg, checked its description, original-file link, source and rights statements, and followed its Sinica database link. The original SVG request was rejected by the browser as unsupported content type. The Commons page for Shuowen_Seal_Radical_422.svg returned an internal error, so it was not selected.

gaps: The cited 《合集》 inscription identifiers are not individually dated on the inspected CUHK page; they support early attestation but not a precise first date.
The Academia Sinica evolution page lists script stages and an indexed bronze witness but does not expose image-level dates in parsed text. No glyph image was visually inspected in this research.

No evidence located here establishes a fixed early design, a single date when a top stroke was added, or graphic corruption. CUHK describes variation among early forms; the dossier’s simple ‘top stroke added later’ statement remains unconfirmed.
Commons file Shuowen_Seal_Radical_422.svg could not be inspected, so its identity, direct image link and reuse terms remain unverified.

items.period: Small seal / Shuowen seal-script style; Commons labels it Shuowen seal style, without dating the particular digital drawing.
items.tradition: Chinese small seal script (modern digital vector reconstruction)
items.caption: Modern vector reconstruction of 雨 in a Shuowen seal-script style, showing a later standardized rendering of the rain graph.
items.alt: A modern black-line vector drawing of the Chinese character 雨 in a seal-script style.
items.selection_reason: Provides a sourced seal-style comparison point following the early variable forms described by the paleographic entry. It is explicitly a digital reconstruction, not an ancient artifact image.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public-domain dedication stated on the exact Commons file page; original file link was verified there.

limitations.text: Only a seal-style reconstruction is proposed. No ancient oracle-bone or bronze image is selected because the inspected Academia Sinica page did not expose a verified direct glyph image URL, and no artifact image was visually inspected.
